title: The four asset classes and their jobs
objectives: Name the four main asset classes and the job of each.
Give an example product for each class.
body_md:
There are four main asset classes, and each has a different job.

| Asset class | Main job | Typical behaviour | Example products |
|---|---|---|---|
| Equity | Long-term growth, beating inflation | Highest long-run growth; sharp falls along the way | Equity mutual funds, PMS, direct stocks |
| Debt | Stability and income | Steadier; carries interest-rate and credit risk | Debt funds, bonds, FDs, PPF, EPF |
| Gold | Diversifier, crisis hedge | Often holds up when equity falls; long flat spells | Gold ETFs, gold funds, SGBs already held |
| Cash | Liquidity and emergencies | Very stable; often below inflation after tax | Savings account, liquid funds |

## The point of the table

No single class does every job. Equity without debt swings too hard for most clients. Debt alone loses to inflation. Gold alone can be flat for a decade. Cash is there so a bad month never forces a sale.

The mix is how these jobs are combined for one client and one goal.
example: A retiree's emergency fund sits in cash, her three-year expense pot in debt, and the money she will not touch for fifteen years in equity and gold. Four classes, four different jobs, one client.
say: Equity is for growth, debt for stability, gold as a diversifier and cash for liquidity.
Each asset class has a job; the mix is how we combine them.
never: Gold always goes up when markets fall.

talk_track.title: Four asset classes, four different jobs
talk_track.text: There are four main asset classes, and each has a different job. Equity is for growth: it has the highest long-run growth, but with sharp falls along the way. Debt is for stability and income: it's steadier, though it carries interest-rate and credit risk. Gold is a diversifier: it often holds up when equity falls, but it can go through long flat spells. And cash is for liquidity and emergencies: very stable, but often below inflation after tax.

check.q: Which asset class is mainly for long-term growth?
check.why: Equity has the highest long-run growth, with sharp falls along the way.

check.q: What is gold's main role in a portfolio?
o: A diversifier that often holds up when equity falls
check.why: Gold is a diversifier and crisis hedge, and it can go through long flat spells. Usually 5–15% is enough.

check.q: Why hold cash at all, when it often trails inflation?
o: So a bad month never forces a sale of long-term investments
check.why: Cash buys liquidity and emergencies, so nothing long-term has to be sold at the wrong moment.
